instructions: Rinse 1 1/2 cups of jasmine rice under cold water until it runs mostly clear. Transfer it to a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups of water and bring it to a boil. Cover, turn the heat to the lowest setting and cook for 12 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on until you serve.

Meanwhile, cut the tofu into 1 inch cubes and pat them very dry with paper towels. Quarter the mushrooms and mince the shallots and the garlic. Slice the green onions thinly and keep the white and green parts apart. Slice the cucumbers into rounds.

Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat for 1 minute. Add the tofu in a single layer and leave it alone for 4 minutes, until the underside is golden. Turn the cubes and cook for 4 minutes, until they're golden on most sides.
Transfer the tofu to a plate. Pour off all but 1 tsp of the oil from the skillet.
Turn the heat to medium. Add 3 tbsp sugar and 1 tbsp of water. Don't stir. Swirl the skillet now and then for 4 to 6 minutes, until the sugar turns the color of dark honey.
Add the shallots and the white parts of the green onions and stir for 30 seconds. Add the garlic and stir for 10 seconds.
Stand back a little. It will spatter. Add 3/4 cup of water, 3 tbsp tamari and the pepper. The caramel may harden at first. Stir for 1 minute, until it melts into the sauce.
Add the mushrooms and the tofu. Cover and cook over medium-low heat for 10 minutes, stirring once halfway through.
Uncover and cook for 3 minutes, until the sauce is thick and clings to the tofu. Take the skillet off the heat and stir in the green parts of the green onions.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch of salt.
Serve with the rice and the cucumber.
method_notes: Both versions fry the tofu first, cook sugar to a caramel, then loosen it with water and a salty seasoning before simmering the tofu and mushrooms in it with plenty of black pepper. The lead (Full of Plants) uses vegan fish sauce or soy sauce; this uses tamari so it stays gluten-free. A Vietnamese pineapple version and a tomato version exist as well, but this keeps to the classic peppery caramel braise. No source had 20 or more ratings, and the lead is the best-rated one that could be read.
